Tara — thanks for the clear note and the PDF. Pasting answers below and copying our billing lead Ben and AR for final sign-off.

Short answers up front:
- We can accept payment in EUR for this invoice. Please use the EUR account shown in the attached "Redwood_Wire-Instructions-EUR.txt" file; include Invoice #8342 in the payment reference.
- Redwood policy: default is SHA (shared) for cross-border intermediary fees; we do not automatically gross-up for correspondent-deducted intermediary fees. In practice we handle exceptions case-by-case (see concession note below).

Details / next steps:
- If you originate an EUR wire to our EUR account (IBAN: ... in the instructions attachment) and include the invoice reference, it normally posts cleanly without downstream conversion. If your bank performs an on-the-fly USD conversion before sending (i.e., your bank sends USD onward), that can be routed through additional correspondents and may introduce deductions.

- If your payment arrives net of intermediary fees, we can either: (a) accept the net amount and apply it to the invoice (then issue a separate credit/adjustment if agreed), or (b) you can re-initiate the payment with SHA but instruct your bank to use OUR routing to ensure gross delivery (note OUR can be refused by some banks).

- To avoid surprises, please ask your bank to confirm they will send "EUR credited to beneficiary account in full" and list the full IBAN/beneficiary name from our attachment. If they insist on converting to USD on their side, please ask for a correspondent chain and estimated fee so we can advise.

Ben — can you confirm if AR will automatically issue a credit when intermediary deduction is under $30, or should we escalate?

Thanks,
Irene

Hi Tara — quick from AR. Thanks for flagging. A couple of practical notes: 

1) Our preferred flow for EU customers is to pay into our EUR IBAN (attachment) so no cross-currency conversion is required. That avoids most correspondent/deduction issues.

2) If a payment posts short because of an intermediary deduction, our default is NOT to automatically credit the customer for those bank-level correspondent fees. We typically request evidence (SWIFT trace / MT103) and then review. For customer relationships above $100k ARR we will consider absorbing a single small deduction (< EUR 25) as a one-time concession.

3) Typical advice to your bank: use SHA if they cannot do OUR. If they use SHA, itemize the intermediary deduction and provide an MT103 so we can reconcile quickly. If they use OUR but the intermediary still deducts, please supply the trace and we will investigate with our bank.

Workflow: please send the MT103 / SWIFT confirmation once the payment is sent. If the invoice remains short we will either post a credit (AR) or invoice you for the shortfall depending on the agreed concession.

Adding Marissa for visibility since this touches payment terms for the deal.

—Ben
Director, Accounts Receivable
Redwood Inference
